chunk: IT Security & Acceptable Use Policy (EN, 202501) # IT Security & Acceptable Use Policy Version: 202501 Company: Global Service Firm Region: Global (EN)

The purpose of this IT Security & Acceptable Use Policy is to establish guidelines for the secure use of company technology resources. This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and thirdparty users who access company devices, networks, cloud services, and thirdparty tools.
Laptops and desktops Mobile devices (smartphones, tablets) Personal devices under BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) policy
Companyowned networks Remote access via VPN Public WiFi connections
Approved cloud applications (e.g., Google Workspace, Microsoft 365) Thirdparty tools and services

Regularly update software and applications. Use strong, unique passwords for different accounts. Example: An employee receives a prompt to update their software and neglects it. This could lead to vulnerabilities that cybercriminals exploit.

Report any suspicious activity or security incidents immediately to IT. Example: An employee notices unusual login attempts on their account and reports it, allowing IT to take action before any damage occurs.
Complete mandatory security training annually. Manager Checklist: Ensure all team members complete training. Schedule followup sessions for those who miss deadlines.
Minimum of 12 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. Change passwords every 90 days.
MFA is required for all critical systems.
Use SSO where available to streamline access and enhance security.

Employees are encouraged to use companyapproved password managers. Enable encryption on all devices. Use screen locks to prevent unauthorized access.

Ensure personal devices comply with company security standards. Example: An employee uses their personal tablet for work but fails to enable encryption. This could expose sensitive data if the device is lost.
Regularly update operating systems and applications. Manager Checklist: Verify that team members' devices are encrypted. Ensure all devices are patched regularly.
Always connect to the company VPN when accessing company resources remotely.
Avoid accessing sensitive information over public WiFi networks. Example: An employee accesses their email over a public WiFi network at a coffee shop, risking exposure to data interception.
Access to company resources from highrisk locations is prohibited. Manager Checklist: Remind team members of VPN usage. Monitor compliance with public WiFi restrictions.

Confidential: Sensitive company data (e.g., financial records) Internal Use Only: Nonpublic information (e.g., internal reports) Public: Information available to the general public (e.g., marketing materials)
Store data in approved locations only. Use secure methods for sharing sensitive information.
Follow data retention schedules as outlined in the Data Retention Policy.
Implement DLP measures to monitor and protect sensitive data. Manager Checklist: Ensure team members understand data classification. Monitor compliance with storage and sharing guidelines.
Use only companyapproved cloud applications.
Avoid using unauthorized applications that could expose company data.
Securely store and manage API keys. Manager Checklist: Review team usage of cloud applications. Educate team on risks of shadow IT.
Be vigilant against phishing attempts. Do not click on suspicious links or attachments.

Autoforwarding of company emails to personal accounts is prohibited. Example: An employee receives an email that appears to be from IT requesting login credentials. Recognizing it as a phishing attempt, they report it instead of responding. Manager Checklist: Conduct regular phishing simulations. Remind team members of autoforwarding rules.
Grant access based on the principle of least privilege.
Follow established protocols for onboarding, role changes, and offboarding employees.
Regularly audit access rights to ensure compliance. Manager Checklist: Review access rights quarterly. Ensure compliance with the joinermoverleaver process.
User activity on company devices and networks. Email and messaging for compliance.
To protect company assets and ensure compliance with policies.
Monitoring data is retained for a period of 12 months.
Any unauthorized access, data breaches, or suspicious activity.
Use the designated incident reporting system.
Report incidents within 24 hours of discovery.
Classify incidents as Priority 1 (P1) or Priority 2 (P2) based on severity. Manager Checklist: Ensure team members know how to report incidents. Review incident response procedures regularly.
Conduct risk assessments before granting access to third parties.
Ensure all third parties sign nondisclosure agreements.
Immediately revoke access when no longer needed. Manager Checklist: Review thirdparty access quarterly. Ensure NDAs are in place for all vendors.
Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary actions, up to and including termination. Each case will be reviewed individually, considering the severity of the violation.

1. What should I do if I forget my password? Use the password reset feature or contact IT for assistance. 2. Can I use my personal device for work? Yes, but it must comply with the BYOD policy. 3. What constitutes a security incident? Any unauthorized access or suspected data breach. 4. How often should I change my password? Every 90 days, as per company policy. 5. What should I do if I receive a suspicious email? Do not click any links and report it to IT immediately. 6. Are we allowed to use cloud services not approved by the company? No, using unauthorized applications is prohibited. 7. How is employee activity monitored? Activity on company devices and networks is monitored to ensure compliance and security.  This policy is designed to protect both the company and its employees by ensuring a secure and responsible use of technology resources. Compliance with these guidelines is mandatory.
